Geely's EX2 Subcompact Hatchback Celebrates Sales Milestone, 1 Million Units Moved in 2 Years
55 photos
Photo: Geely
The Chinese automaker that controls Volvo, Polestar, Lotus, and plenty other marques is celebrating a sales milestone that cements the core brand on the worldwide stage. Geely's latest global success may not come with a desirable badge, tremendous power, or the high driving position of a crossover, yet the EX2 has passed one million cumulative sales.
So what? Many nameplates did exactly that, and Toyota comes to mind with the Corolla. To date, just around 58 million were delivered worldwide, making the Corolla the best-selling automotive nameplate of them all. Regarding the EX2, which is otherwise known as E2 in a bunch of markets, one million sales in merely two years is what makes this milestone stand out.
The big mil was reached in October 2026, a month in which Geely sold a grand total of 71,337 units. All told, averaging one sale every minute in the past couple of years is truly impressive for a vehicle the US market has not experienced. If you ask me, that's even more outstanding when you remember that Geely is the kind of auto brand most of us continue to dismiss as just another Chinese newcomer.
Geely Automobile Holdings Limited of Hangzhou, Zhejiang, launched the EX2 in October 2024, and customers wasted little time getting their own EX2s. The full-electric hatchback reached 10,000 sales within 16 days, then crossed 200,000 deliveries after little more than 200 days. The 600,000th sale was clocked on its 536th day. Commercially successful, alright!
The 2025 result, namely its first full year on sale, was particularly spectacular. No fewer than 465,775 were moved in total, making it the best-selling passenger car in China across all segments and the world's top seller in both the A and B segments. Based on its footprint, the EX2 is more subcompact than city car.
Photo: Geely By October 2026, its maker had introduced the rear-drive hatchback in more than 30 markets across Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific region, and Latin America. The question is, what made the EX2 so appealing in so many places that could not be more diverse in terms of customer preferences?
I, for one, like cheap and cheerful vehicles as much as the next person. Honest vehicles are rare nowadays, and I also like its warranties. As far as the battery is concerned, and this is the biggest concern you can have with a fully electric vehicle, Geely provides an eight-year warranty up to 200,000 kilometers (124,274 miles). Said warranty applies to the general vehicle as well.
Over those eight years or 200,000 clicks, the battery warranty guarantees at least 70 percent of the original capacity. Regarding prices, how do you feel about 90 euros per month through financing or 99 euros per month via leasing? Retail prices, meanwhile, kick off at 19,990 euros in Germany. That's the largest new car market in Europe, and two grand over the Dacia Spring for a lot more car and standard equipment sounds like a great deal.
Equipped with a multi-link rear suspension instead of a cheapo torsion-beam setup, the EX2 offers 70 liters (2.5 cubic feet) in the front trunk and very flexible rear cargo space. Its quoted turning radius makes it perfect in the urban jungle, and better still, customers are not forced to compromise where it actually matters.
Those who do little, mostly urban driving are presented with a smaller battery (35.35 kWh) that provides 252 kilometers (157 miles) in the WLTP, while customers who need more driving range in one go can opt for a 47.14-kWh pack that promises up to 345 kilometers (214 miles). In both cases, fast charging from 30 to 80 percent should take 25 minutes.
As it stands, Geely and the EX2 now have to prove that the next million will come just as easily as Chinese rivals bring increasingly competitive small EVs to showrooms worldwide. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Geely Australia | New Energy Vehicles (@geely.auto.australia)
